question: Discrimination of MCI from cognitively normal (healthy) controls with structural T1 MRI in ADNI older adults. AD vs CN is also a shared contrast. The ledger's comparison is a misreading (condition 6): it sets P-109's three-class 96.81% against an '~82%' that P-66 does not print, and P-109 reports no binary AD-vs-MCI result. The pair is therefore judged on the contrasts both papers print. The cohorts differ (P-109 3T subset of 1,075; P-66 1.5T Siemens Symphony subset of 599), as do the input representation and the split unit; the rule allows these differences.
metric: accuracy with accuracy (and AUC with AUC)

figures.P-109: MCI/HC (BrainViT-L, Table 4): accuracy 94.23%, AUC 0.9715, from a random 90/10 split of shuffled 2D slices (about 50 per subject). The MCI/HC task has 685 subjects (370 MCI, 315 HC), and the number of test subjects is not reported. Taking the conservative n = 69 (10% of 685), Wilson 95% CI 0.861-0.977; with n = 685, 0.922-0.957. AUC by Hanley-McNeil with 37/32: SE 0.020, CI 0.932-1.000. AD/HC: accuracy 97.13% (Wilson n = 70: 0.902-0.992), AUC 0.9852.
figures.P-66: MCI vs CN (radiomics+CNN fusion, Table 6): accuracy 72.7% +/- 3.3 (SD over 5 folds), AUC 0.80 +/- 4.6, from 400 subjects (200 MCI, 200 CN; 1,801 images). Wilson with n = 400: 0.681-0.768. AUC by Hanley-McNeil with 200/200: Q1 = 0.80/1.20 = 0.667, Q2 = 2(0.64)/1.80 = 0.711, SE 0.022, CI 0.757-0.843. AD vs CN: accuracy 84.4% (Wilson n = 399: 0.805-0.876), AUC 0.90.

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists. P-109 reports no hippocampus/amygdala ROI result, no 1.5T result and no subject-level split; P-66 reports no whole-brain-input result. The nearest figures inside each paper leave the gap open. P-109's own ResNet50 baseline on its slice split reaches MCI/HC 85.13% (AUC 0.9411), still outside P-66's interval. P-66's best single-ROI model is below its fusion (hippocampus 71.5%). P-109's Table 7 cites a third study (a hippocampus-segmented 3D DenseNet, MCI/HC 76.20%); that is another paper's result on other data, not either paper's result under the other's condition.
performance_validity: Borderline for P-109. P-66 passes (at most AUC 0.90). P-109's discrimination is at or above 0.97 on internal validation only (MCI/HC AUC 0.9715, AD/HC AUC 0.9852 and accuracy 97.13%, three-class AUC 0.9805), with no external cohort. Its split shuffles slices randomly, about 50 per subject, before the 90/10 division, which is the subject-bleed design Section 3.5 names as a candidate mechanism. However, the Section 3.5 rule is conjunctive, and its small-sample clause is not met on a literal reading: the study has 1,075 subjects, 685 in the MCI/HC task. Read literally, P-109 is not excluded and the pair qualifies. If the rule is read as covering near-ceiling results from a split without subject separation, the pair fails condition 5.

candidate_explanations.difference: Input representation: whole-brain 2D slices in three planes vs segmented hippocampus and amygdala ROIs
candidate_explanations.quote: For training and testing, around 50 brain fields—axial, coronal, and sagittal—were created from each subject’s anatomy.
we aimed to develop an algorithm based on CNN and radiomic features derived from ROIs of bilateral hippocampus and amygdala in brain MRI for stratification between AD, MCI and CN.

candidate_explanations.difference: Split unit: random slice-level shuffle (about 50 slices per subject) vs random image-level partition (948 images from 200 MCI patients); neither separates subjects, and P-109's design places far more of each subject on both sides
candidate_explanations.quote: The images were shuffled randomly, and all experiments were carried out by splitting the data into 10 % for testing and 90 % for training.
randomly dividing the MRI data for each classification dataset into a sizeable training and validation set (80 % of images) and a testing set (20 % of images).

candidate_explanations.difference: Scanner and ADNI subset: 3T vs 1.5T Siemens Symphony
candidate_explanations.quote: All sMRI scans were conducted at a resolution of 3Tesla (3 T)

candidate_explanations.difference: Architecture and capacity: a hybrid CNN-transformer (20.1M parameters) vs radiomics plus a small ROI 3D CNN. P-109's own ResNet50 on the same split reaches only 85.13% for MCI/HC, so architecture accounts for part of the gap on P-109's data but not for the remainder down to 72.7%.

candidate_explanations.quote: A total of 1075 individuals, including 390 with AD, 370 with MCI, and 315 HC, were used to create a balanced dataset for the 2D model.

reason: Both papers classify MCI against controls from ADNI T1 MRI and print incompatible results: 94.23% (CI 0.861-0.977 even at the conservative test n) against 72.7% (CI 0.681-0.768), with AUCs of 0.9715 and 0.80. No figure in either paper reconciles them. The only condition in doubt is 5. P-109's near-ceiling AUCs come from internal validation with a random slice-level split and no external cohort, but its 1,075-subject sample does not meet the rule's small-sample clause as written. If that clause is applied literally, the pair qualifies, with input representation, split unit, scanner field strength, architecture and sample size as candidate explanations, none shown to be sufficient.

quotes.quote: The images were shuffled randomly, and all experiments were carried out by splitting the data into 10 % for testing and 90 % for training.
For training and testing, around 50 brain fields—axial, coronal, and sagittal—were created from each subject’s anatomy.
A total of 1075 individuals, including 390 with AD, 370 with MCI, and 315 HC, were used to create a balanced dataset for the 2D model.
BrainViT-L, exhibited higher accuracy, surpassing other models, with rates of 97.13 % with 98.52 % AUC for AD/HC and 94.23 % with 97.15 % for MCI/HC classifications

In the term of MCI vs CN, radiomic-based algorithm alone obtained ACC of 71.6 % and AUC of 77.8, CNN-based algorithm obtained ACC of 69 % and AUC of 75 and their fusion showed ACC of 72.7 % and AUC of 80.

We randomly selected baseline structural MRI data (T1-weighted images) from a total of 2403 images of 599 different individuals, including 853 images of 200 cases with cognitively normal controls (CN), 602 images of 199 patients with AD, and 948 images of 200 patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) at baseline.
The performance evaluation method employed in this study was the 5-fold cross-validation method.
The major limitation of this study was the single-center limitation.
